title: Wishing and going
hook: shoes by the door, a ride you keep meaning to take; Shantideva splits the awakening mind in two
tomorrow: nothing to give. so what does Shantideva offer?

segments.voice: Yesterday: the alchemist's elixir. The wish to wake up for everyone turns base metal to gold, starting with whoever you are. Today Shantideva admits a wish can sit on a shelf.
screen: `BASE METAL TO GOLD.` → `A WISH CAN SIT ON A SHELF.`

segments.voice: There's a pair of running shoes by somebody's door right now, laces still tied from the store. The owner really does want to run. They've looked up routes. They've thought about it on the bus. And the shoes haven't moved. Wanting to go has its own feeling, warm and hopeful. Going has a different one: cold air, the slap of a sole on the sidewalk, the first breath that's a little too hard. Shantideva knew those were two different things.
screen: `SHOES BY THE DOOR, LACES TIED.` → `WANTING HAS ONE FEELING.` → `GOING HAS ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: In his first chapter, he says the awakening mind comes in two kinds. One is the mind that wishes: the resolve to wake up for the sake of everyone. The other is the mind that sets out: actually walking that road, one act at a time. Then he gives the picture himself. Look at the difference, he says, between someone who wants to go somewhere and someone who is going. The wise, he says, see the same difference here. What's surprising is that he doesn't throw the wish away. He says even the wishing mind brings great good. It points you somewhere. A person who never wanted to go never goes. But it isn't the same as setting out. Only the going, he says, keeps good flowing steadily, even while you sleep or your mind wanders. So the two aren't rivals. The wish is the map. The going is your feet on the road. That's the end of chapter one: the awakening mind, from lightning to a road. For today, a small rule: wish, then go.
screen: `THE MIND THAT WISHES.` · `THE MIND THAT SETS OUT.` · `WANTING TO GO, AND GOING.` · `THE WISH IS THE MAP; GOING IS THE ROAD.` · then, large: `WISH, THEN GO.`

segments.voice: Stand up and walk slowly, anywhere, even across one room and back. With each step, feel the heel touch, then the ball of the foot, then the push away. If standing is hard, press each foot into the floor in turn. Let the wish to go be in your head, and let your feet do the going.
Wishing and going: Shantideva's two kinds of awakening mind. The resolve to wake up for all, and actually setting out on the road.
Keep this: wish, then go, because the shoes only matter once they move. Chapter one, walked to its end.
